records.name: Friends of Carpenters Woods
records.summary: Volunteers who care for Carpenters Woods. Recent work days included weeding the meadow and repairing the bridge, and the group posts work day news on its own website.
records.what_you_do: Join a work day to weed the meadow, repair the bridge and other structures, and help look after the woods. The group's website also shares a bird guide, a tree map, and plant information.

schedule.text: Work days are held several times a year and announced in blog posts. The site gives no fixed days or times.

first_step.how: Email focw24@gmail.com and ask about the next volunteer work day
first_step.basis: Work days are announced in blog posts without dates on the site, and no sign-up steps are published, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Tier 1 had status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10, which was the check date, not a dated item. The group's own site (focw.org) was not known to tier 1, which saw only Facebook. Its newest dated post is March 10, 2026 (spring volunteer day), so status is active. Work day dates, times and meeting places are not published, so first visit detail is limited. The contact page also gives a mailing address, 236 W Gorgas Lane, 19119. The one web search returned mostly a Chorleywood (England) Carpenters Wood, which was ignored. Facebook not read. Partner Friends of the Wissahickon is in leads_only.

records.name: Friends of Carroll Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Carroll Park in West Philadelphia. They began meeting in 2018 to join the City's Park Friends network, and in 2020 they ran socially distanced exercise sessions and joined park cleanup days. We found no newer public updates.
records.what_you_do: In 2020 the group ran socially distanced exercise sessions, shared census and voter registration information, and joined Love Your Park cleanup days.

first_step.how: Email carrollparkfriends@gmail.com and ask whether the group is still meeting
first_step.basis: The only way in is an email to ask whether the group still meets, and the newest public post about its activity is from 2020.

records.notes: Tier 1 had status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10. Neither is supported: the newest dated evidence is an October 13, 2020 Philadelphia parks blog post, so status is dormant. The group's only web presence is Facebook, which was not read. The City Park Friends page lists the email but no website. The verdict stays publish because the group is on the City list and has a public email, but someone should confirm it still meets before it is promoted.

records.name: Friends of Cianfrani Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Cianfrani Park at 8th and Fitzwater. The group's blog has posted about cleanups, tree care, planting, and gardening workshops, and it holds a monthly meeting. Its newest dated post is from 2021.
records.what_you_do: Its past posts describe park cleanup days, tree care, planting, gardening workshops, and requests for donations. The group meets on the first Tuesday of each month, at Palumbo Recreation Center or in the park when the weather allows.

schedule.text: The group meets at 7 pm on the first Tuesday of each month, at Palumbo Recreation Center at 10th and Fitzwater, or in the park when the weather allows.

first_step.how: Go to the first-Tuesday meeting at 7 pm at Palumbo Recreation Center (10th and Fitzwater), or email Cianfranipark@gmail.com to confirm the group still meets
first_step.basis: The site lists a monthly meeting time and place, but its newest dated post is from 2021 and it gives no sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Tier 1 had status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10, which was not supported. The group's blog's newest dated post is November 14, 2021 (donations), and its cleanup and tree posts run from 2017 to 2021. Each post also shows a second date, September 16, 2026, the same on every post, which looks like a site update stamp rather than an event, so it is not used as evidence. Status is dormant. The monthly meeting is stated on the site but could not be confirmed as current. The park meetings page URL returned 404. The site names no volunteer sign-up. Whether meetings are open to the public is not stated; open_to public is carried over from tier 1. Facebook not read.

records.name: Friends of Clark Park
records.summary: Neighbors who support Clark Park in West Philadelphia. They push for the park upgrades the City approved, such as nature-based playgrounds and a permanent restroom, and they host events such as Parktoberfest.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers help with gardening, social media outreach, and tabling at the Saturday farmers market. Members pay yearly dues, and anyone can ask for access to the online board meetings.

schedule.text: The group keeps a membership table at the Saturday farmers market. Volunteers sign up by email, and board meetings are held online.

cost.text: Yearly dues start at $10 for seniors, students, and people with limited income, and are $25 for an individual. A one-time donation is also accepted.

first_step.how: Stop by the membership table at the Saturday farmers market, or email volunteer@friendsofclarkpark.org to ask about volunteering
first_step.basis: The membership table and volunteer email are public and say how to join; the site does not say newcomers are welcome in so many words.
first_step.what_to_expect: You can stop at the membership table at the Saturday farmers market to join or ask about volunteering. Dues are yearly: $10 at the lowest level and $25 for an individual. Board meetings are held online, and access is given on request by email to the president.
first_visit_tips: Online membership sign-up asks for a birthdate, and you must be over 13 to join online.
Ask about the board meeting link by emailing the president through the group's Board Meetings page.

records.notes: Tier 1 wrote Parktoberfest as Saturday October 10 with 2026 inferred from the weekday. The notice prints no year, and October 10 is a Saturday in other years too, so that date was removed from schedule and was not used for last_sign_of_life. The newest post with a printed year is 'We Walk PHL Fall 2026' (post dated September 9), which is now last_sign_of_life. The newest post overall, Parktoberfest (September 15), prints no year. The calendar page lists no events and no feed. Board meeting dates are not published. The volunteer and membership pages give a group office address of 4300 to 4398 Baltimore Ave, 19104; the park location is kept as 4301 Chester Ave. Online membership sign-up requires users to be over 13. Facebook and Instagram not read. Partner programs named on the site are in leads_only.

records.name: Friends of Cloverly Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Cloverly Park in Northwest Philadelphia. They hold Love Your Park work days in May and November, look after the park's trees, and work to protect the Old Tennis Court Farm.
records.what_you_do: Join a May or November work day, pick up litter, or help with garden weeding and upkeep through the growing season. Cash donations are accepted any time, and some years the group holds a plant sale.

schedule.text: Love Your Park work days run on Saturday mornings in May and November, 10 am to 1 pm, at Cloverly Park. Garden upkeep continues through the growing season.

cost.text: No fee is listed for work days. Cash donations are accepted any time by mailed form.

first_step.how: Register for the next May or November work day through the group's contact page or the Love Your Park registration form
first_step.basis: Work days are open to volunteers of all ages and abilities, and the page says how to register, but it does not say beginners are welcome in so many words.
first_step.what_to_expect: A work day runs 10 am to 1 pm on a Saturday in May or November at Cloverly Park. The tasks are litter pickup, weeding, and general upkeep. Volunteers of all ages and abilities are welcome.
first_visit_tips: Register ahead, since service days need registration.
Contact the group before joining garden work, as the page asks.

records.notes: Tier 1 had status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10, which was the check date. Corrected from the events page, which prints the year: it lists a Spring 2026 Love Your Park Work Day on Saturday, May 9, 2026, so last_sign_of_life is 2026-05. records.name: Friends of Courtesy Stable
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs a riding stable near the Wissahickon in Fairmount Park, offering riding lessons, leasing, and boarding. It also holds monthly volunteer days for barn and park upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Come to a volunteer day, which the site describes as monthly with no dates posted, to help with park and barn work. You can join the free barn mailing list for volunteer openings, or take riding lessons. The riding page lists trail rides only as a perk of a lease, and leasing is open to current students.

schedule.text: Volunteer days are described as monthly, with no dates on the site; the events calendar is linked from the events page. Lessons run year round and are booked by email when a slot opens.

cost.text: Lessons are paid, with prices given on request, and are due the day of the lesson unless paid in advance by cash or check. Barn Days cost $50 per person. Joining the barn mailing list is free.

requirements.gear: Hard-soled shoes with a heel. A helmet is required whenever you are mounted, and one can be borrowed.

first_step.how: Sign up for the free barn mailing list, which carries barn news and volunteer openings, or email barnmanager@courtesystable.org to ask about a lesson
first_step.basis: Lessons are booked by email and held until a slot opens, and the site gives no volunteer dates, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: A lesson is one hour, either private or shared with other riders, and you choose how often you ride. Before you ride you must sign the rider release form, which you can download and complete ahead of time. Riders under 15 need a parent or guardian on site, and lesson payment is due the day of the lesson, by cash or check, unless paid in advance.
first_visit_tips: Wear hard-soled shoes with a heel.
Bring a helmet, or ask to borrow one, since a helmet is required whenever you are mounted.
Download and complete the rider release form before you arrive.
Plan for parking, which is both on-street and off-street.

access.notes: Parking is on-street and off-street, and the barn has one restroom.

records.notes: Tier 1 had status active and last_sign_of_life 2026-10, which was the check date. No dated item with a printed year appears in the last 12 months (the riding page shows only a 2024 copyright, which does not count), so status is probably_active: a working site with no dated items, and last_sign_of_life is omitted. Corrections to tier 1: trail rides are a lease perk only, not a standalone option. The legal name on the site is Boarders and Stewards of Courtesy Stable, a 501(c)(3); the City list uses the Friends name. Minimum rider age is 8; under 8s are referred to Sandy Hill Farm. The minimum age applies to riding, and no age limit is stated for volunteer days. Two emails are published: barnmanager@courtesystable.org for lessons and cynbarn0421@gmail.com in the site header; the record keeps the second as contact email. Volunteer day dates are on an events calendar linked from the events page, which was not opened because its link is not in the page text. Barn hours on the contact page are listed as 9 am to 8 pm, with a note to contact the stable for availability, so they are not used. Facebook and Instagram not read.

notes: Seven groups. Own sites read: Clark Park (6 fetches), Cloverly Park (6), Courtesy Stable (6), Carpenters Woods (focw.org, 2), Cianfrani Park (cianfranipark.com, 2), Carroll Park (one 2020 blog post, its only site is Facebook), Fairview Park (none; its domain redirects to Facebook). Status corrections against tier 1: tier 1 put the check date (2026-10) into last_sign_of_life for most groups, which is not dated evidence. Result: Clark Park active (2026-09), Cloverly active (2026-05), Carpenters Woods active (2026-03), Courtesy Stable probably_active (working site with no dated items), Carroll Park dormant (2020-10), Cianfrani Park dormant (2021-11), Fairview unknown. The batch brief treats all seven as alive, which the evidence does not support for Carroll Park and Cianfrani Park; please review before they go live. Partner organizations not in the batch are in leads_only.
